why: Interview practice: design questions with numbers, trade-offs explained in writing, and a few small programs where code teaches the idea.

sd-ip-addresses.why: address sizes and private ranges are recall; the DNS task uses them

sd-dns.why: why a changed record still sends some users to the old server is a behaviour to explain

sd-dns-records.why: a short list of record types; the DNS routing design uses them

sd-dns-routing.why: routing policy, health checks and TTL are chosen with numbers for a scenario

sd-http.why: choosing methods and status codes, and which calls are safe to repeat, is reasoning, not recall

sd-latency-throughput.why: Little's law and the latency/throughput split are numbers to work out

sd-rest.why: shaping resources, statelessness and pagination for a concrete API is a design exercise

sd-rpc.why: REST versus RPC is a trade-off interviewers ask you to explain

sd-interview-framework.why: the order of the interview steps is recall; the requirements and API tasks exercise it

sd-requirements.why: turning a vague prompt into requirements and a read/write ratio is the opening move of a design answer

sd-api-design.why: sketching endpoints, pagination and auth for a prompt is a design exercise

sd-data-model.why: entities, keys and access patterns are designed for a prompt, with sizes

sd-estimation-method.why: seconds per day and powers of two are used in estimates, not memorised

sd-qps-estimate.why: average and peak QPS are numbers to estimate from a scenario

sd-storage-estimate.why: storage per year with retention is a number to estimate

sd-bandwidth-estimate.why: ingress and egress bandwidth are numbers that drive a design decision

sd-high-level-design.why: drawing the simplest design that meets the requirements is a design exercise

sd-bottlenecks.why: naming the bottleneck from estimates and stating the trade-off is a written answer

sd-timed-walkthrough.why: a time budget to follow; the mocks practise it

sd-performance-vs-scalability.why: telling a performance problem from a scalability one is explained from symptoms

sd-vertical-horizontal-scaling.why: scale up versus scale out is a trade-off to argue

sd-stateless-services.why: where session state goes and why sticky sessions hurt is a trade-off to explain

sd-load-balancers.why: health checks, TLS termination and a redundant pair are placed in a design

sd-lb-algorithms.why: weighted round robin and least-connections are small algorithms to implement and compare

sd-l4-vs-l7.why: choosing layer 4 or layer 7 routing for given needs is a trade-off to explain

sd-reverse-proxy.why: forward versus reverse proxy is a definition; the load balancer tasks use it

sd-cdn.why: origin offload from the hit ratio is a number that shapes the design

sd-push-pull-cdn.why: push or pull for a given content set is a trade-off to argue

sd-api-gateway.why: gateway versus load balancer, and aggregation for mobile, is a trade-off to explain

sd-rate-limiting.why: a small per-key rate limiter that answers 429 with Retry-After teaches what limiting means

sd-scale-to-millions.why: sizing each tier from the traffic that reaches it is a numbers-first design

sd-cache-basics.why: hit ratio and effective latency are numbers to work out

sd-cache-layers.why: mostly a map of where caches sit; the cache-aside task uses it

sd-cache-aside.why: a cache-aside read path is a small program to write and test

sd-cache-invalidation-ttl.why: a TTL cache with delete-on-write shows staleness bounds in tests

sd-read-write-through.why: read-through and write-through costs are trade-offs to explain

sd-choose-cache-strategy.why: choosing a pattern and TTL from the read/write ratio is a design decision

sd-distributed-cache.why: local versus global cache and the remap burst are weighed with numbers

sd-relational-acid.why: what a transaction protects in a transfer is a behaviour to explain

sd-denormalization.why: denormalising for reads versus keeping copies in sync is a trade-off to explain

sd-nosql-base.why: definitions of NoSQL families and BASE; the store choice task uses them

sd-key-value-store.why: what a key-value store suits is recall; the store choice task uses it

sd-document-store.why: what a document store suits is recall; the store choice task uses it

sd-wide-column-store.why: partition and clustering keys are designed for a query shape

sd-object-storage.why: where media bytes and their metadata live is a design decision

sd-sql-vs-nosql.why: matching each entity to a store from its access pattern is a design exercise

sd-replication-leader-follower.why: what happens to reads and writes when the leader dies is a behaviour to explain

sd-sync-async-replication.why: sync versus async replication is a durability-latency trade-off to explain

sd-replication-lag.why: why a user cannot see their own write, and the fix, is a predict-and-explain answer

sd-consistency-models.why: which consistency each feature needs is a trade-off to argue

sd-cap-theorem.why: what a store gives up during a partition is explained per feature

sd-quorum.why: choosing N, W and R is arithmetic plus a trade-off

sd-partitioning-basics.why: definitions of partitioning kinds; the shard key task uses them

sd-sharding-strategies.why: range versus hash versus directory sharding is a trade-off to explain

sd-shard-key.why: picking a shard key and handling a hot key is a design decision

sd-consistent-hashing.why: a hash ring with binary-search lookup is a small program, and remap counts are testable

sd-storage-design-choice.why: store, replication, shard key and consistency are chosen together for a prompt

sd-sync-vs-async.why: what a caller gains and loses by going async is a trade-off to explain

sd-message-queues.why: backlog growth and drain time are numbers to work out

sd-task-queues-background-jobs.why: moving work off the request path, and job retries, are explained for a case

sd-back-pressure.why: wait time from backlog and where to reject are worked out with numbers

sd-pub-sub.why: queue versus topic for a new consumer is a choice to explain

sd-delivery-guarantees.why: acknowledging before or after processing, with a crash, is simulated in a few lines

sd-idempotency.why: one definition; the idempotency key task exercises it

sd-idempotency-keys.why: an idempotency-key store and an idempotent consumer are small programs to test

sd-polling-long-polling.why: request rate and delay of polling are numbers to compare

sd-websockets.why: sizing connection servers by open connections is a numbers question

sd-realtime-at-scale.why: routing a message to the right connection server is designed end to end

sd-fan-out.why: fan-out writes per second decide write versus read fan-out

sd-availability-nines.why: downtime budgets are numbers to work out

sd-availability-series-parallel.why: series and parallel availability are computed for a design

sd-single-points-of-failure.why: finding and removing single points of failure is done on a concrete design

sd-health-checks-heartbeats.why: detection time against false alarms is tuned with numbers

sd-failover.why: active-passive versus active-active and the data lost on failover are explained

sd-timeouts.why: a timeout is set from the dependency's p99 and the caller's deadline: numbers

sd-retry-backoff-jitter.why: a retry loop with capped exponential backoff and jitter is a small program to test

sd-circuit-breaker.why: a breaker's closed, open and half-open states are a small state machine to implement

sd-sagas.why: compensating steps and orchestration versus choreography are explained for a flow

sd-monitoring-observability.why: the signals and golden signals are recall; the failure review uses them

sd-security-overview.why: where authentication and authorization are checked is explained for a request

sd-reliability-review.why: walking a design's failure modes with an availability figure is a design exercise

sd-case-url-shortener.why: the classic case: code length, cache and redirect choices with numbers

sd-case-news-feed.why: fan-out, timeline cache and storage split are designed with numbers

sd-case-chat.why: connection routing, ordering and offline delivery are designed end to end

sd-geohash.why: encoding a location as a geohash is a small program with checkable output

sd-case-ride-hailing.why: location write load, matching and double dispatch are designed with numbers

sd-mock-method.why: how to run and score a mock; the mocks themselves are the practice

sd-mock-url-shortener.why: a timed mock is itself a design answer

sd-mock-news-feed.why: a timed mock is itself a design answer

sd-mock-chat.why: a timed mock is itself a design answer

sd-mock-ride-hailing.why: a timed mock is itself a design answer

sd-mock-unseen-prompt.why: an unseen prompt is the final design answer
